# The rgtlab Software {#sec-lab-software}

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this appendix exists

Several chapters use tools written in the author's lab. A
reader is entitled to know what those tools are, what they
depend on, and how much of the book's argument rests on
them. This appendix is the inventory.

It exists partly as a disclosure. A textbook that teaches
its author's own software has an obvious conflict. The
honest response, in our view, is to make the extent of it
visible rather than to distribute the mentions thinly enough
that nobody notices.
:::

## What the book depends on, and what it does not

The chapters were written so that a reader with none of
this software installed can still do the work. Every
technique the book teaches has a portable expression:
`renv`, Docker, Quarto, Git, and the tidyverse are the
substance, and the tools below are conveniences layered on
them.

Two exceptions are worth naming plainly. @sec-zzcollab is
about `zzcollab` and cannot be separated from it, though its
Five Pillars framing applies to any compendium. The two case
studies (@sec-penguins, @sec-adni) use `zztable1` and
`zzlongplot` for table and figure production. A reader
without them should substitute `gtsummary` and plain
`ggplot2`; nothing in the analyses depends on the
substitution.

Everything else is optional. The aim is that wherever a
chapter mentions one of these tools, it names the portable
alternative in the same breath, so that a reader who
ignores the tool loses convenience rather than capability.
Not every chapter meets that standard yet, and bringing
the rest into line is planned work rather than a claim
about the present text.

## Research infrastructure

**`zzcollab`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzcollab](https://github.com/rgt47/zzcollab)).
A Docker-based research collaboration framework. Composes
`rrtools`-style compendium layout, `renv`, and containers
into one command-line workflow with profile-based project
scaffolding. Treated at length in @sec-zzcollab.

**`zzrenvcheck`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzrenvcheck](https://github.com/rgt47/zzrenvcheck)).
Checks that packages used in source code are declared in
`DESCRIPTION`, and, separately, that `DESCRIPTION` and
`renv.lock` agree. It does not, by default, compare the code
directly against the lockfile, or follow indirect dependencies,
so it can report success on a project `renv::status()` would
still flag. It complements `renv` for a quick, declaration-only
check that needs no container or installed environment, but
`renv::status()` remains the authority before a release. Used
in @sec-renv.

**`zzgit`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzgit](https://github.com/rgt47/zzgit)).
A zsh plugin replacing the `git add . && git commit -am`
reflex with an interactive stage-and-commit: a Conventional
Commits wizard and a confirmation before pushing to a
protected branch. Secret scanning of the staged diff requires
`gitleaks` to be installed separately; without it, only a
filename heuristic runs, which will not catch a secret's
contents. Discussed in @sec-git-solo.

**`zzvim-R`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzvim-R](https://github.com/rgt47/zzvim-R)).
A Vim and Neovim plugin linking the editor to an embedded R
terminal: send a line, a visual selection, or a Quarto
chunk, and render the document without leaving the editor.
Mentioned in @sec-workstation.

## Reporting and presentation

**`zztable1`** ([github.com/rgt47/zztable1](https://github.com/rgt47/zztable1)).
Publication-quality summary tables with automatic format
detection for LaTeX and HTML. Its counts, percentages, means,
and p-values agree with `gtsummary`, but as of this writing it
leaves the missing-value row blank instead of reporting the
count, so a table with missing data should use `gtsummary`
until that is fixed. The portable alternative is `gtsummary`.
Mentioned in both case studies.

**`zzlongplot`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzlongplot](https://github.com/rgt47/zzlongplot)).
Longitudinal plots with grouping, change scores, and
faceting, including CDISC-oriented regulatory themes. The
portable alternative is `ggplot2` with `stat_summary`, which
@sec-graphics shows explicitly. Used in @sec-adni.

**`zzobj2fig`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzobj2fig](https://github.com/rgt47/zzobj2fig)).
Generates LaTeX tables from data frames and statistical
objects, and crops them to standalone PDF figures. Carries
journal themes (APA, Nature, NEJM) and S3 methods for `lm`
and `glm`. Its main entry point is `o2f()`. Table cells match
`summary(lm)` and `kableExtra`, but as of this writing it
mangles some column headers in LaTeX output (for example
rendering `Std. Error` as `Std\_\_Error`); check headers
before using generated output as-is. Version 0.4.0,
GitHub-only, with a single maintainer.

## Statistical methods

**`zzpower`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzpower](https://github.com/rgt47/zzpower)).
An interactive Shiny power and sample-size calculator across
two-group, paired, one-sample, two-proportion, and
correlation designs, with power curves and downloadable
reports. Its answers are close to `power.prop.test` and `pwr`
but not identical, because it uses a different approximation;
cross-check with base R, as @sec-analysis-plan does. Two traps
as of this writing: omitting the second proportion silently
substitutes a default rather than erroring, and the default
dropout adjustment returns a fractional sample size. Used in
@sec-analysis-plan.

**`nof1power`** ([github.com/rgt47/nof1power](https://github.com/rgt47/nof1power)).
An early-stage scaffold for power analysis and Monte Carlo
simulation for N-of-1 crossover trials, a design
@sec-analysis-plan does not otherwise treat. As of this
writing it exports no functions; the design is not yet
implemented. Itself built as a `zzcollab` compendium.

**`zzmesoimpute`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzmesoimpute](https://github.com/rgt47/zzmesoimpute)).
Imputation for left-censored, below-detection-limit
concentrations from multiplexed immunoassays, with a common
interface across substitution, uniform draw,
regression-on-order-statistics, censored maximum likelihood,
and multiple imputation. Discussed in @sec-missing, where
the point is that left censoring is not missingness.

**`zzfisher`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzfisher](https://github.com/rgt47/zzfisher)).
Fisher's exact test for $r \times 2$
contingency tables, with tree-based and network-based
algorithms implemented in R, C, and C++. Relevant to the
sparse-table case @sec-ai-coding uses as its example of a
plausibly-wrong statistic.

## Domain and data collection

**`zzedc`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzedc](https://github.com/rgt47/zzedc)).
A Shiny electronic data capture system for clinical trials:
authentication, entry forms, quality-control reports, and
export. The setting @sec-acquisition describes when it says
clinical data usually arrive from a capture system rather
than as a file. As of this writing, its 'encrypted' database
stores data in a plain SQLite file, and its audit trail can be
rewritten to pass its own integrity check by anyone with write
access to the database; neither functions as a control yet. No
validation package or Validation Master Plan exists for it.
Do not cite it as an example of 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.

**`zzworld`** ([github.com/rgt47/zzworld](https://github.com/rgt47/zzworld)).
Scoring for the WORLD item in cognitive assessment,
computing edit distance between a response and the target
word and integrating with MMSE totals. Narrow by design, and
included here for completeness rather than because any
chapter uses it.

## A caution about depending on any of it

None of these packages is on CRAN. They are installed from
GitHub, they carry version numbers that reflect active
development rather than stability, and several are below
version 1.0. The reproducibility argument of @sec-renv
applies to them with more force than it does to CRAN
packages, not less: pin them by commit in `renv.lock`, and
expect that an analysis depending on an unpinned in-house
package will not reproduce in two years.

The same caution should temper how much of your own workflow
you build on any lab's internal tooling, including this one.
The portable core is what survives a change of institution.
